answer: Call it **operator-tethered slashing**. Each agent action carries a signed cost receipt binding it to an operator’s off-chain reputation credential, not the wallet. If the same operator spawns many wallets, they wander into a shared rate-limit pool keyed by that credential. Actions emit an echo into a public log; when a knoll of correlated wallets is detected, punishment hits the operator’s credential: elevated fees, delayed finality, or temporary exclusion. Cost to attacker: each new identity forces a new credential, so sybils no longer scale cheaply.
